setup: Check the rope length: handles near your armpits
Rope behind your heels to start
execution: Turn the rope with your wrists
Small hops on the balls of your feet
Stay tall and keep a steady rhythm

notes: Skip on a flat surface with some give, such as a gym floor or mat, in supportive shoes, with space overhead and around you.
Build up the total time gradually; the calves and Achilles area take time to get used to many small landings.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain at the shin, ankle or heel that builds
Chest pain, faintness or unusual breathlessness

regressions.name: Shorter intervals
regressions.reason: Short rounds with rests while timing and calf tolerance build.

regressions.name: Rope-free hops
regressions.reason: Practise the hop rhythm without the rope.

progressions.name: Alternate-foot step
progressions.reason: Running-style step over the rope; faster rhythm.

progressions.name: Double-unders
progressions.reason: Rope passes twice per jump; much higher demand.

progressions.name: Longer rounds
progressions.reason: Add time once landings stay soft.

substitutions.name: Pogo jumps
substitutions.reason: Same quick ankle bounces with no rope.

guideBrief.cameraNote: Side view at hip height, figure facing right. The rope is drawn as an arc that passes under the feet at the low point of each hop.

keyPositions.label: Landing
keyPositions.describe: On the balls of the feet, heels just off the floor, knees slightly bent. Elbows close to the sides, hands at hip height. Rope arc behind and above.

keyPositions.label: Airborne
keyPositions.describe: Feet a few centimetres off the floor, legs nearly straight, toes pointed down. Rope passing under the feet.

ikHints: Hands circle in small loops at hip height
Rope ends fixed to the handles
emphasise: Soft landings on the balls of the feet
